We need to output a test class code that includes tests for all cases per JSON. Use parameterized tests. The framework already has a single test debug_shouldLogMessageWithCorrectPatternAndArguments. But we need to expand to cover groups.

We can create parameterized tests with MethodSource providing arguments; each case includes logger mock (or null), node mock (or null, or special etc), rootNode mock, at string (including null). For cases expecting exception, we assertThrows.

Need to create mocks for JsonNode, but also for cases where node throws exception on toString. Use Mockito's when(node.toString()).thenThrow(new RuntimeException(...)). However SLF4J formatting uses {} placeholders and will call node.toString() to evaluate when logger.debug is called? In SLF4J, logger.debug(String, Object...) uses param substitution without calling toString if logger.isDebugEnabled? In our mock logger, we just verify debug method called with given arguments; not actual formatting. However in exceptionThrowingNode case, they assume exception occurs when formatting. But with mock logger, calling logger.debug with node argument will directly pass node as object; no toString. However if logger.debug implementation uses node.toString internally, but we mock logger; we can stub logger.debug to call real method? Actually using mock logger, its debug method is stubbed returns void and doesn't evaluate args, thus no exception from node.toString. To simulate exception we can make logger.debug call invocation arguments' toString. We can do when(logger.debug(anyString(), any(), any(), any())).thenAnswer(invocation -> { // evaluate args
Object arg1 = invocation.getArgument(1);
arg1.toString(); // may throw
Object arg2 = invocation.getArgument(2);
arg2.toString();
Object arg3 = invocation.getArgument(3);
arg3.toString();
return null;
}); This will cause exception if node/rootNode throws.

Similarly for logger null we just pass null reference, method will cause NPE when trying to call logger.debug; we just call method and expect NPE.

We also need cases where logger.debug throws RuntimeException or AssertionError; we can stub logger.debug to throw.

Thus we need separate test methods for different expectation groups or combine parameterized and use dynamic expected outcome.

Simplify: create parameterized method for normal cases (no exception) where we verify logger.debug invocation and arguments.

Then other parameterized for exception expectations.

Better to use @MethodSource and create mocks inside test method using parameters such as strings for identifiers then instantiate inside test. Simpler: in test method, use switch-case based on caseId.

But we can create a helper method to build case data.
